title: Intake Air Heater Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the intake air heater. This part warms incoming air so a diesel engine starts easily in the cold.
symptoms: White smoke right after a cold start

causes.name: Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the intake air heater wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the intake air heater with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new intake air heater if it tests bad.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit/Open
plain: The computer feeds a steady 5-volt supply to a group of sensors, and supply "A" has dropped out or is not reaching the sensors. Several sensors can stop reading correctly at once.
symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time

causes.name: Shorted sensor on the shared 5-volt circuit (such as a throttle, pedal or pressure sensor)
Chafed or damaged wiring shorted to ground

checks: Note which other sensor codes set at the same time
Unplug sensors on that circuit one at a time and watch whether the 5-volt supply comes back
Inspect the harness for rubbing, melting or water damage
fix: Usually finding and replacing the sensor that is shorting the supply, or repairing damaged wiring.

cost.job: Find and repair shorted sensor or wiring

drive: Get it checked soon. This fault can knock out several sensors at once, causing limp mode, stalling or a no-start. If power drops sharply or the engine stalls, stay out of heavy traffic and consider a tow.
test_first: Unplug sensors on the shared 5-volt "A" circuit one at a time to find a short, and check wiring for chafing and connectors for water before replacing the computer.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit Low
plain: The computer feeds a steady 5-volt supply to a group of sensors, and supply "A" is being pulled too low, usually by a short to ground. Several sensors can stop reading correctly at once.
symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time

causes.name: Shorted sensor on the shared 5-volt circuit (such as a throttle, pedal or pressure sensor)
Chafed or damaged wiring shorted to ground

checks: Note which other sensor codes set at the same time
Unplug sensors on that circuit one at a time and watch whether the 5-volt supply comes back
Inspect the harness for rubbing, melting or water damage
fix: Usually finding and replacing the sensor that is shorting the supply, or repairing damaged wiring.

title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit High
plain: The computer feeds a steady 5-volt supply to a group of sensors, and supply "A" is too high, usually from a short to another voltage source. Several sensors can stop reading correctly at once.
symptoms: Several sensor codes at the same time

causes.name: 5-volt supply wire shorted to a higher voltage
Faulty sensor on the shared circuit
Corroded connector letting moisture bridge pins

checks: Note which other sensor codes set at the same time
Unplug sensors on that circuit one at a time and watch whether the 5-volt supply comes back
Inspect the harness for rubbing, melting or water damage
fix: Usually finding and replacing the sensor that is shorting the supply, or repairing damaged wiring.

title: Driver Display Serial Communication Circuit
plain: The engine computer is having trouble sending information to the driver display, such as the instrument cluster or message center.
symptoms: Gauges or dash messages missing or wrong

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem on the display data line

checks: Scan all modules for communication codes
Inspect wiring and connectors behind the cluster
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a cluster or display repair.

title: A/C Clutch Relay Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem, such as a broken connection, in the circuit it uses to control the A/C clutch relay. This part switches the A/C compressor clutch on and off.
symptoms: A/C compressor not engaging or never shutting off

causes.name: Broken wire or loose or corroded connector

checks: Inspect the A/C clutch relay wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the A/C clutch relay with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new A/C clutch relay if it tests bad.

title: A/C Clutch Relay Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer sees lower voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the A/C clutch relay, often from a wire shorted to ground. This part switches the A/C compressor clutch on and off.
symptoms: A/C compressor not engaging or never shutting off
checks: Inspect the A/C clutch relay wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the A/C clutch relay with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new A/C clutch relay if it tests bad.

title: A/C Clutch Relay Control Circuit High
plain: The computer sees higher voltage than expected in the circuit that controls the A/C clutch relay, often from a wire shorted to power or a failed part. This part switches the A/C compressor clutch on and off.
symptoms: A/C compressor not engaging or never shutting off

causes.name: Faulty or shorted A/C clutch relay

checks: Inspect the A/C clutch relay wiring and connector for damage or corrosion
Check related fuses and relays
Test the A/C clutch relay with a meter or scan tool and compare with spec
fix: Usually a wiring or connector repair, or a new A/C clutch relay if it tests bad.

title: Immobilizer Lamp Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem in the circuit it uses to turn on the security (immobilizer) light on the dashboard.
symptoms: The security (immobilizer) light may not work or may stay on

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem between the computer and the instrument cluster

checks: Check whether the security (immobilizer) light comes on during the startup bulb check
Inspect wiring between the computer and the cluster
fix: Usually a wiring or instrument cluster repair.

title: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem in the circuit it uses to turn on the cruise control light on the dashboard.
symptoms: The cruise control light may not work or may stay on

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem between the computer and the instrument cluster

checks: Check whether the cruise control light comes on during the startup bulb check
Inspect wiring between the computer and the cluster
fix: Usually a wiring or instrument cluster repair.

title: Fuel Pump Control Module
plain: The module that controls the fuel pump reported a fault, so the pump may not run correctly.
symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start

causes.name: Corroded connector or damaged wiring at the module
Low voltage or poor ground to the module
Faulty fuel pump drawing too much current

checks: Check the fuel pump control module connector for corrosion
Check module power, ground and fuel pressure
fix: Usually a new fuel pump control module or a wiring repair.

title: PTO Control Module
plain: The module that controls power take-off (used to run equipment on work trucks) reported a fault.
symptoms: Power take-off equipment may not work

causes.name: Low voltage or poor ground to the module

checks: Check module power and ground
Inspect wiring and connectors to the PTO system
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new PTO control module.

title: Glow Plug Control Module
plain: The module that powers the diesel glow plugs reported a fault.
symptoms: White smoke after a cold start

causes.name: Corroded connector or poor ground at the module

checks: Test the glow plugs and their wiring
Check module power, ground and connectors
fix: Usually a new glow plug control module or glow plug, or a wiring repair.

title: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1
plain: The part of the engine computer that reads the oxygen sensors on bank 1 failed a self-check.

causes.name: Shorted oxygen sensor or heater wiring
Low voltage or poor power and ground connections
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement (a new one usually must be programmed to the car).

title: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance Bank 2
plain: The part of the engine computer that reads the oxygen sensors on bank 2 failed a self-check.

causes.name: Shorted oxygen sensor or heater wiring
Low voltage or poor power and ground connections
Computer software that needs an update

checks: Test the battery and charging system
Check the computer power and ground circuits and connectors
Check for manufacturer software updates or service bulletins
fix: Fix any power or ground problem first; otherwise the computer may need reprogramming or replacement (a new one usually must be programmed to the car).

title: Unauthorized Software/Calibration Detected
plain: The engine computer found software that wasn't approved by the manufacturer, such as an aftermarket performance tune.
symptoms: Engine may not start or may run in limp mode on some vehicles

causes.name: Aftermarket tune or performance programmer installed

checks: Ask whether the vehicle has been tuned
Reflash the computer with factory software
fix: Reflash the computer with the correct factory software.

title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp (MIL) Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem in the circuit that turns on the check engine light itself.
symptoms: Check engine light does not come on at key-on, or stays on
May fail an emissions or safety inspection

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem to the instrument cluster

checks: Check whether the check engine light comes on with the key on and engine off
Inspect wiring between the computer and the cluster
fix: Usually a wiring, bulb or instrument cluster repair.

title: Engine RPM Output Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem in the circuit that sends engine speed (RPM) to the tachometer or other modules.

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem in the RPM output circuit
Faulty instrument cluster or receiving module

checks: Check whether the tachometer works
Inspect wiring between the computer and the cluster
fix: Usually a wiring or cluster repair.

title: Engine Hot Lamp Output Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem in the circuit it uses to turn on the engine overheat warning light on the dashboard.
symptoms: The engine overheat warning light may not work or may stay on

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem between the computer and the instrument cluster

checks: Check whether the engine overheat warning light comes on during the startup bulb check
Inspect wiring between the computer and the cluster
fix: Usually a wiring or instrument cluster repair.

title: Fuel Level Output Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem in the circuit that sends the fuel level reading to the fuel gauge or other modules.
symptoms: Fuel gauge wrong, stuck or not working

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem in the fuel level output circuit

checks: Compare the gauge with the fuel level on a scan tool
Inspect wiring between the computer and the cluster
fix: Usually a wiring or cluster repair, or a new fuel level sender.

title: Actuator Supply Voltage "A" Circuit/Open
plain: The power feed the computer uses for parts like injectors, solenoids and valves (supply "A") is missing or broken.
symptoms: Stalling, no start or limp mode
Several other codes may set at once

causes.name: Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the actuators
Shorted actuator or chafed wiring pulling the supply down

checks: Check fuses and relays that feed the engine actuators
Inspect the harness for chafing or melted wires
Unplug actuators one at a time to find a short
fix: Usually a fuse or relay, a wiring repair, or a shorted part.

title: Actuator Supply Voltage "A" Circuit Low
plain: The power feed the computer uses for parts like injectors, solenoids and valves (supply "A") is too low.
symptoms: Stalling, no start or limp mode
Several other codes may set at once

causes.name: Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the actuators
Shorted actuator or chafed wiring pulling the supply down

checks: Check fuses and relays that feed the engine actuators
Inspect the harness for chafing or melted wires
Unplug actuators one at a time to find a short
fix: Usually a fuse or relay, a wiring repair, or a shorted part.

title: Actuator Supply Voltage "A" Circuit High
plain: The power feed the computer uses for parts like injectors, solenoids and valves (supply "A") is too high.
symptoms: Stalling, no start or limp mode

checks: Check fuses and relays that feed the engine actuators

title: Generator System Performance
plain: The alternator isn't putting out the charging the computer is asking for.
symptoms: Dim lights or a battery that keeps going dead

causes.name: Loose or corroded battery or alternator connections

checks: Test charging voltage with lights and blower on
Inspect the drive belt and tensioner
Check alternator and battery connections
fix: Usually a new alternator, belt or a connection repair.

title: Generator Control Circuit Range/Performance
plain: The computer's control signal to the alternator isn't producing the expected result.
symptoms: Dim lights or a battery that keeps going dead

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem at the alternator

checks: Test charging voltage
Inspect the alternator connector and wiring
fix: Usually a new alternator or a wiring repair.

title: Generator Mechanical Performance
plain: The alternator doesn't seem to be turning or working properly mechanically, often from belt slip or a failing alternator.

causes.name: Worn, loose or slipping drive belt

checks: Inspect the drive belt and tensioner
Spin the alternator pulley by hand with the belt off to feel for roughness
fix: Usually a new belt or tensioner, or a new alternator.

title: Reductant System Malfunction Lamp Control Circuit
plain: The computer found a problem in the circuit for the diesel exhaust fluid (DEF) warning light.
symptoms: DEF warning light not working or stuck on

causes.name: Wiring or connector problem to the instrument cluster

checks: Check whether the DEF light comes on during the startup bulb check
Inspect wiring between the computer and the cluster
fix: Usually a wiring or cluster repair.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Performance Bank 1
plain: The valve inside the intake manifold (bank 1) that changes how air flows to the engine at different speeds isn't moving the way the computer expects.
symptoms: Slight loss of power at some engine speeds

causes.name: Vacuum leak to a vacuum-operated actuator

checks: Watch whether the valve or actuator moves when commanded
Check the actuator vacuum hose and linkage
fix: Usually a new tuning valve actuator, or an intake manifold if the valve is built in.

title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Performance Bank 2
plain: The valve inside the intake manifold (bank 2) that changes how air flows to the engine at different speeds isn't moving the way the computer expects.
symptoms: Slight loss of power at some engine speeds

causes.name: Vacuum leak to a vacuum-operated actuator

checks: Watch whether the valve or actuator moves when commanded
Check the actuator vacuum hose and linkage
fix: Usually a new tuning valve actuator, or an intake manifold if the valve is built in.
